messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High tail latency detected for MercuryCorp - dedicated pool 'mercury-prod-1'. P99 generator CPU and token queueing spikes. Auto-escalation -> paging oncall.

maria (oncall): Ack. Jumping in. paging log shows sustained token backlog on node g-12.

sam (eng-sre): I'm 2nd. Oncall, handoff to me if you need model-level changes. What’s the approximate impacted qps?

maria (oncall): ~450 qps sustained over 5m, error rate ~1.8%  (500s and gRPC timeouts). Top routes: /v1/generate and /v1/chat.

leo (infra): Node g-12 reports GPU mem pressure + kernel preemption messages in dmesg. NVLink flaps briefly. I’m attaching a quick debug snippet:

```
$ kubectl logs --tail=100 runtime-g-12
[...OOM warnings...]
TensorRT executor WARN: out-of-memory, attempting fallback
Queue length: 320
```

sam (eng-sre): Suggest isolating noisy tenant and activating throttle policy for MercuryCorp’s shard to protect the pool. Also consider fallback model variant with smaller sequence length.

maria (oncall): Agreed. Taking step 1: route new requests to fallback model `redwood-small-v1` for MercuryCorp for 10m rolling window. Applying policy now.

incident-bot: Command executed: `route set --customer mercurycorp --pool mercury-prod-1 --model redwood-small-v1 --ttl 600`

maria (oncall): Throttle enabled: `rate-limit mercurycorp 350r/s` and KV prefix cache flush for their hot prefixes.

mercury-eng: We see improved latency on some requests. But a subset of long-context calls still spike. We do have a scheduled long-context job from yesterday; could that be it?

sam (eng-sre): Checking recent workloads. Found a cron job hitting /v1/chat with seq len 16k starting at 02:10 UTC. That will blow up KV and cause kernel fallbacks. Can we pause? @mercury-eng please confirm.

mercury-eng: Confirm pause initiated for the job. Thanks.

leo (infra): NVLink errors reduced after pausing job. GPU mem regained. Queue down to ~40. P99 latency trending toward normal.

anya (cust-success): Preparing customer comms. ETA 15m for an initial note. Need confirmation on impact window and mitigation actions to include.

sam (eng-sre): Impact window start: 02:05 UTC, mitigation applied 02:18 UTC (route + throttle + job pause). Recommend noting temporary model fallback and throttle; no data exfiltration.

maria (oncall): Running post-mit checks for stability. If stable for 20m, we can start a controlled revert to main model and gradually lift throttles.

incident-bot: Pager update: incident severity set to P2 -> active mitigation in progress.

(20m later)

maria (oncall): Stability hold reached. Rolling revert: route set back to `redwood-prod-v2` in canary (10%) for MercuryCorp. Monitoring.

sam (eng-sre): Revert looks fine so far. No kernel warns. Gradually increasing to 100% over next 7m.

leo (infra): Confirming pool metrics look normal. No further NVLink events.

anya (cust-success): Drafting initial customer message: "We observed elevated latency on your dedicated pool due to a long-context job causing GPU pressure. We paused the job, applied a temporary model fallback and rate limits, and restored normal service within 20 minutes. We’re preparing an RCA and will propose credits as needed." OK to send?

maria (oncall): OK to send after we attach the impact times and final mitigation timeline.

exec-ops: Heads-up — MercuryCorp is enterprise tier. Recommend offer of 10% monthly credits for this incident pending RCA. Please include finance contact.

anya (cust-success): Noted. I’ll include proposed credit and request approval from finance.

sam (eng-sre): Action items:
- sam: draft RCA root cause + timeline (initial).
- leo: attach infra logs & NVLink trace.
- maria: confirm exact token counts and final metrics.
- anya: customer comm send + credit proposal.
- exec-ops: confirm credit authorization workflow.

maria (oncall): Starting RCA draft now. Key point: long-context cron job from customer exceeded expected seq length; kernel preemption cascaded to out-of-memory fallbacks. Suggest adding quota for long-context jobs per-customer on dedicated pools.

mercury-eng: Appreciate quick mitigation and the pause. We’ll add an internal guard to prevent scheduled jobs from scaling to 16k seq without an opt-in.

incident-bot: Incident resolved -> state: mitigation complete, monitoring. Closing bridge in 10m unless new alerts.

anya (cust-success): Sent initial comm to MercuryCorp with impact window, mitigations, and proposed 10% credit. Customer acknowledged and asked for RCA draft.

(Post-incident, later that day)

sam (eng-sre): Uploaded RCA draft to /shared/incidents/1766554321-rca.md. Core findings + recommended long-term controls: per-customer long-context quota, model autoscaling limits, and improved KV cache eviction heuristics.

exec-ops: Approved proposed 10% credit pending legal review. Finance looped in.

anya (cust-success): Scheduling exec sync with MercuryCorp for tomorrow 14:00 UTC to walk through RCA and remediation roadmap.

maria (oncall): Closing out runbook items and patching the pool config to include a default long-context throttle.

mercury-eng: Thanks all. Appreciate the quick ops.

incident-bot: Thread archived.
